title: 5.3 Would you like some tea?
unit_outcome: Say how much and how many, offer and order food and drinks politely, agree about likes, say what you want and need to do, talk about meals, prices and what is in your food, compare prices, use numbers to ninety-nine and ask for things at the table.
goal: Offer a drink with Would you like some …? and accept or refuse it (Yes, please. / No, thank you.).
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 5.3 Drinks: A1 names drinks and says who drinks them, and A1 5.10 answers an offer with Yes, please. / No, thank you.; A1+ 5.3 makes the offer: Would you like some + a drink? It is one new frame, learnt as a whole (would is not taken apart), with A1+ 4.15's some; hot chocolate and lemonade are the new drinks (lemonade added 2026-11-23). In each photo a host holds out a drink and the guest takes it or holds up a hand, so the photo shows the reply. The asker's voice always differs from the answerer's (Ana and Sofia share one voice, as do Luis and Diego). I'd like waits for 5.9.
prerequisite: A1 5.3 tea, coffee, water; A1 5.10 Yes, please. / No, thank you.; A1+ 4.15 some; A1 5.5 I like.
speaking_outcome: Say Would you like as one phrase (WOOD-ja-LIKE is fine) with rising intonation at the end of the offer; do not require native-like speed.
